When SpaceX isn't launching unmanned rockets, it turns out it's been busy acquiring artificial intelligence companies. In February this year, the company that owns Starlink quietly acquired xAI, which also owns Twitter, later renamed X. In April, SpaceX struck a deal with Cursor, a competitor to Claude Code and OpenAI Codex. As of August 14, the acquisition has been completed. The company has now been renamed SpaceXAI, and with Cursor's assistance, it recently launched the Grok Bot and the Grok 4.6 model.

Updated August 14, 2026: SpaceXAI has completed its acquisition of Cursor.

Updated June 16, 2026: SpaceX acquired Cursor just one week after going public.

Below is the original report with updates:

SpaceX strikes $10 billion Cursor deal paving way for subsequent $60 billion acquisition

Cursor has long been popular among software engineers who write AI programs on Mac, and was one of the earliest services to connect large language model AI to the application development workflow.

In April, the two companies stated that SpaceX and Cursor were "working closely together, with the goal of building the world's best AI for coding and knowledge work."

The initial collaboration agreement included SpaceX paying Cursor $1 billion:

In April, before the acquisition, Cursor further disclosed details of the collaboration:

Cursor is working with SpaceX to accelerate our model training efforts. Composer is the first agentic coding model we've released in six months. Afterwards, Composer 1.5 will scale up reinforcement learning by more than 20 times. Composer 2 further adds continuous pre-training to achieve frontier-level performance at a cost far lower than other models. Every increase in computing resources brings significant gains in model capability. We have always wanted to further advance our training efforts, but were previously limited by computing resources. Through this partnership, our team will leverage xAI's Colossus infrastructure to dramatically enhance the intelligence of our models.

SpaceX's collaboration with Cursor has strengthened the competitiveness of a competitor to Anthropic's Claude Code and OpenAI Codex agentic coding software.
